title: Chanan the Egyptian
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: According to the Gemara, [Ketubot 105a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.105a.2-4), he was one of the judges of decrees in Jerusalem in Temple times, with Admon and Chanan, and Hyman says that he is not mentioned in the Mishnah. In Yoma 63a (compare [Yoma 63b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.63b.7)): “Chanan the Egyptian says: Even if the blood is in the cup, he brings its fellow and pairs it.” Hyman distinguishes another Chanan the Egyptian who lived in the time of Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues, as in Sanhedrin 17a (compare [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.4)): “They discussed before the sages: Shimon ben Azzai, Shimon ben Zoma and Chanan the Egyptian.”[^1]

notes.text: [Mishnah Ketubot 13:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Ketubot.13.1) names Admon and Chanan ben Avishalom. The linked Gemara adds Chanan the Egyptian and explains the terminology for the judges. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1402&lang=en) also distinguishes the two Chanans in the Ketubot discussion. The linked Sanhedrin list includes Chananya ben Chachinai as well. Hyman’s distinction between the Yoma and Sanhedrin notices remains his.
